outputs.L1: An assembly apparatus according to an embodiment of the present technology includes a work base, a first robot, a second robot, and a controller. The work base includes a placement surface on which a plurality of workpieces are placed and is configured to individually circulate the workpieces among a plurality of work areas arranged along a circumference at predetermined time intervals. The first robot is disposed inside the circumference and is capable of accessing the plurality of work areas. The second robot is disposed outside the circumference and is capable of accessing at least one of the plurality of work areas. The controller causes the first robot to perform a predetermined process, within each predetermined time interval, on workpieces located in a plurality of predetermined work areas among the plurality of work areas. outputs.L2: In one implementation of the present technology, an assembly system comprises a work platform, first and second robots, and a control unit. The platform includes a support surface carrying multiple workpieces and, at fixed time intervals, moves each workpiece among several processing regions positioned around a circular path. The first robot is located within this path and can reach all of the processing regions. The second robot is positioned outside the path and can reach at least one of those regions. During each fixed interval, the control unit directs the first robot to execute a specified process on workpieces located in multiple designated processing regions. It also directs the second robot to assist the first robot’s process by performing an operation on the workpiece in at least one of the designated regions.
outputs.L3: The assembly apparatus includes a work base, a first robot, a second robot, and a controller. The work base supports a plurality of workpieces and periodically circulates the workpieces among multiple work areas arranged along a circumference. The first robot is positioned inside the circumference and is configured to access each of the work areas. The second robot is positioned outside the circumference and is configured to access at least one of the work areas. During each circulation interval of the work base, the controller directs the first robot to perform a predetermined process on a workpiece located in a corresponding work area. The controller also directs the second robot to assist the first robot in carrying out the process.
outputs.L4:
The assembly apparatus includes a circulating work base on which one or more workpieces are supported and transported along a predetermined circulation path. A plurality of work areas is arranged at intervals in the circumferential direction of the work base. As the work base circulates, each workpiece is sequentially positioned at the respective work areas, where predetermined operations—such as component supply, positioning, fastening, inspection, or removal—are performed.

An inner robot is disposed on the inner side of the circulation path and is configured to access the workpieces from within the circulating work base. An outer robot is disposed on the outer side of the circulation path and can access the workpieces from the opposite direction. The robots operate under the supervision of a controller that manages movement of the work base, positioning of the workpieces, and execution of the operations assigned to each robot. The controller may coordinate the robots so that they work independently at different work areas or cooperate at the same work area.

At selected work areas, the outer robot assists the inner robot in carrying out an operation that would otherwise require additional time or would be difficult for the inner robot to perform alone. For example, one robot may hold or position a workpiece or component while the other robot performs insertion, fastening, joining, or inspection. The outer robot may also perform a preceding or subsequent operation in parallel with the inner robot, thereby reducing idle time and distributing the processing load between the robots.

The controller assigns operations to the inner and outer robots according to the required processing sequence and the time available during each circulation interval of the work base. Robot motions are synchronized with the movement and stopping positions of the work base to avoid interference and ensure that each operation is completed before the corresponding workpiece advances to the next work area. The controller can further adjust robot assignments in response to production conditions, operating status, or differences in processing time among the work areas.

By selectively using the outer robot to supplement the inner robot, the apparatus completes the predetermined processes within each circulation interval without unnecessarily increasing the number of work areas or extending cycle time. This coordinated arrangement improves assembly efficiency, balances workloads, reduces waiting periods, and enables reliable processing of workpieces throughout the circulating production sequence.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. Saying “a book” could mean any book, while “the book” refers to one that is already known or understood.

Despite its simplicity, “the” brings clarity and focus to communication. It helps readers and listeners distinguish the familiar from the unknown and the particular from the general. This tiny word often goes unnoticed, but without it, everyday language would feel less precise and natural.

“The” is a reminder that even the simplest elements can have an essential role.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an assembly apparatus featuring a circulating work base, an inner robot, an outer assisting robot, and a controller coordinating their operations.
counterfactuals.output: An assembly apparatus includes a circulating work base configured to transport a workpiece along a circulation path, an inner robot disposed inside the circulation path, an outer assisting robot disposed outside the circulation path, and a controller communicatively coupled to the circulating work base, the inner robot, and the outer assisting robot. The inner robot performs one or more assembly operations on the workpiece, and the outer assisting robot supports the assembly operations by supplying, positioning, holding, transferring, or removing a component, tool, or workpiece. The controller coordinates movement of the circulating work base and operation of the inner and outer assisting robots based on a position or operating state of the workpiece, thereby enabling synchronized assembly from opposite sides of the circulation path while reducing interference among the circulating work base and the robots.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an embodiment of an automated assembly system in formal patent language, where multiple workpieces periodically circulate among circumferential work areas and two robots collaborate on processing them.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, an automated assembly system (100) comprises a rotary transport apparatus (110), a plurality of workpiece carriers (112) supported by the rotary transport apparatus (110), a plurality of work areas (120A–120N) circumferentially distributed about the rotary transport apparatus (110), first and second industrial robots (130, 140), and a controller (150) operatively coupled thereto. Each workpiece carrier (112) is configured to retain at least one workpiece (W) in a predetermined position and orientation.

The rotary transport apparatus (110) is selectively driven through a sequence of indexing movements and dwell intervals. During each indexing movement, the workpiece carriers (112), together with the respective workpieces (W), are advanced along a closed circulation path from one circumferential work area to a succeeding circumferential work area. During each dwell interval, the carriers (112) are positioned in registration with respective work areas (120A–120N) to permit performance of one or more processing operations. Repetition of the indexing movements causes each workpiece (W) to circulate periodically among the circumferential work areas.

The first and second robots (130, 140) are arranged such that respective working envelopes thereof overlap at one or more of the work areas. The robots (130, 140) are configured to collaboratively perform an assembly operation on a workpiece located within an overlapping portion of the working envelopes. By way of example, the first robot (130) may engage, locate, support, or reorient the workpiece or a first component, while the second robot (140) retrieves and installs a second component, applies a process material, forms a joint, or operates a fastening tool. In another operating mode, the robots may simultaneously engage different portions of the workpiece to perform coordinated fitting, alignment, fastening, welding, bonding, inspection, or transfer operations.

The controller (150) is programmed to synchronize movement of the rotary transport apparatus (110) with operation of the robots (130, 140). In particular, the controller (150) inhibits entry of either robot into a designated processing region during an indexing movement and initiates a coordinated robotic operation upon confirmation that a selected carrier is stationary and properly registered with the corresponding work area. Position sensors, carrier-identification devices, machine-vision devices, and tool-status sensors may provide feedback to the controller (150), thereby permitting robot trajectories and process parameters to be selected in accordance with the identity, position, or processing state of each workpiece.

The work areas may include, without limitation, loading, component-placement, joining, inspection, rework, and unloading areas. A workpiece may remain on the same carrier during multiple revolutions of the rotary transport apparatus, with the controller maintaining an electronic process record indicating which operations have been completed. A workpiece failing an inspection criterion may accordingly be retained for a subsequent circulation and presented again to the robots for corrective processing, whereas a workpiece satisfying the applicable completion criteria may be discharged at the unloading area.

Accordingly, multiple workpieces may be processed concurrently at different circumferential work areas, while the first and second robots cooperate at one or more selected work areas to perform operations requiring coordinated manipulation, thereby facilitating compact equipment layout, periodic workpiece flow, and flexible allocation of assembly tasks.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain a robotic manufacturing embodiment in which a centrally located robot performs predetermined processes on workpieces within a cycle time while a second, externally located robot assists at one of the processing stations.
counterfactuals.output:
A robotic manufacturing cell may include several processing stations arranged around a central robot. During each production cycle, the central robot moves one or more workpieces between the stations and performs predetermined operations—such as positioning, joining, machining, inspection, or handling—within a specified cycle time.

At one station, a second robot is positioned outside the central robot’s normal work area. This external robot assists with the operation at that station, for example by:

- holding or reorienting the workpiece while the central robot processes it;
- carrying out a second operation simultaneously;
- loading or unloading a tool or component; or
- taking over part of an operation that would otherwise prevent the central robot from meeting the cycle time.

The robots’ controllers coordinate their movements, tool actions, and transfer points to avoid interference. By assigning part of the work at the selected station to the external robot—often in parallel with the central robot’s other tasks—the cell completes all predetermined processes within the required cycle time without needing another complete central processing cell.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
